HON ZHA - Inpatient Cardiology Progress Note
Salient Cardiac Features
71-year-old woman with coronary artery disease, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, type 2 diabetes mellitus, prior right carotid stenting, and history of cerebrovascular accident.
Presented for Lexiscan evaluation because of a history of chest pain and preoperative cardiac assessment. During Lexiscan on 09/02/2026, she developed significant chest pain radiating to the neck with persistent ST-segment depression, prompting hospital admission and coronary angiography. 
Lexiscan perfusion imaging 09/02/2026 demonstrated normal perfusion throughout all myocardial territories without reversible or fixed defects and calculated LVEF greater than 75%. 
Coronary angiography performed by Dr. Obeid/Obed on 09/03/2026 demonstrated no significant proximal coronary stenosis, 60% mid-to-distal LAD stenosis, 60-70% mid first diagonal stenosis, 90% mid-to-distal left circumflex stenosis, 50% proximal RCA stenosis, 50% mid RCA stenosis, and 75% proximal right posterolateral branch stenosis. LV systolic function was normal. No PCI is documented in the provided report. 
Echocardiogram 09/02/2026 demonstrated normal LV systolic function with LVEF 65-70% and no significant valvular disease. Prior echocardiogram 08/10/2026 demonstrated LVEF 60-65%. 
Telemetry demonstrates sinus rhythm.
Cardiac troponin remained without a clinically significant rise during hospitalization. Latest troponin reported during bedside discussion was 0.031 ng/mL.
Current cardiovascular therapy includes aspirin 81 mg daily, atorvastatin 80 mg nightly, amlodipine 5 mg daily, and lisinopril 20 mg daily.
History of right carotid stenting approximately 4 years ago in China.
Patient reassured during bedside discussion. Daughter Kun Yin was not present during bedside evaluation.
SOAP Note
Subjective
Seen in cardiology follow-up after admission for chest pain and significant EKG changes occurring during Lexiscan testing.
Patient subsequently underwent coronary angiography by Dr. Obeid/Obed.
No current chest pain, shortness of breath, or palpitations documented. Patient reports feeling better.
Troponin results and cardiac evaluation were reviewed, and the patient was reassured during bedside discussion.
Daughter Kun Yin was not present during today's bedside evaluation.
Objective
Vitals reviewed elsewhere.
General: Pleasant, alert, and in no apparent distress.
Cardiovascular: Normal S1 and S2 without documented S3 or murmur. Telemetry demonstrates sinus rhythm.
Respiratory: Lungs clear bilaterally without crackles or rhonchi. Most recently documented oxygen saturation 97-99% on room air.
Extremities: No lower-extremity edema. Extremities warm and well perfused with good pedal pulses.
Neurologic: Alert and oriented without documented focal neurologic deficit.
Laboratory Data: WBC 5.4 K/µL, hemoglobin 13.4 g/dL, hematocrit 40.2%, platelets 278 K/µL, sodium 140 mmol/L, potassium 4.4 mmol/L, BUN 20 mg/dL, creatinine 0.67 mg/dL. Latest troponin reported during bedside discussion was 0.031 ng/mL. Hemoglobin A1c 8.2%. LDL 56 mg/dL. 
Relevant Cardiac Procedures/Studies:
08/10/2026 - Echocardiogram demonstrated normal LV systolic function with LVEF 60-65% and no significant valvular disease. 
09/02/2026 - Lexiscan demonstrated normal myocardial perfusion without reversible or fixed defects and calculated LVEF greater than 75%. Despite normal perfusion imaging, the patient developed chest pain with significant persistent ST-segment depression during testing. 
09/02/2026 - Echocardiogram demonstrated normal LV systolic function with LVEF 65-70% and no significant valvular disease. 
09/03/2026 - Coronary angiography by Dr. Obeid/Obed demonstrated 60% mid-to-distal LAD stenosis, 60-70% mid first diagonal stenosis, 90% mid-to-distal left circumflex stenosis, 50% proximal RCA stenosis, 50% mid RCA stenosis, and 75% proximal right posterolateral branch stenosis with normal LV systolic function. No PCI is documented in the provided report. 
Assessment


Coronary artery disease with multivessel coronary stenoses demonstrated by coronary angiography (ICD-10: I25.10)


Chest pain associated with significant EKG changes during pharmacologic stress testing, currently improved (ICD-10: R07.9)


Essential hypertension (ICD-10: I10)


Hyperlipidemia (ICD-10: E78.5)


Type 2 diabetes mellitus without documented complication (ICD-10: E11.9)


History of cerebrovascular accident without currently documented residual neurologic deficit (ICD-10: Z86.73)


History of right carotid artery stenting (ICD-10: Z95.828)


Plan
High-complexity inpatient medical decision-making performed due to symptomatic chest pain with significant EKG abnormalities during pharmacologic stress testing requiring hospital admission and invasive coronary angiography demonstrating multivessel coronary artery disease, with continued cardiovascular risk-factor management and clinical surveillance.
Coronary Artery Disease: Coronary angiography 09/03/2026 demonstrated multivessel coronary stenoses, including 90% mid-to-distal LCx disease, 60% mid-to-distal LAD disease, 60-70% first diagonal disease, 50% proximal and mid RCA disease, and 75% proximal right posterolateral branch disease. No PCI is documented in the available angiography report.
Chest Pain: Symptoms improved. Continue clinical and telemetry surveillance. Patient reassured regarding current findings and clinical status.
Antiplatelet Therapy: Continue aspirin 81 mg PO daily.
Lipid Management: Continue high-intensity atorvastatin 80 mg PO nightly. Most recently documented LDL 56 mg/dL.
Hypertension: Continue amlodipine 5 mg PO daily and lisinopril 20 mg PO daily. Long-term outpatient blood pressure target below 130/80 mmHg has been recommended in view of coronary artery disease and diabetes.
Diabetes: Continue insulin glargine 16 units subcutaneous nightly and insulin lispro correction coverage before meals and at bedtime. Hemoglobin A1c is 8.2%.
Cardiac Function: Preserved LV systolic function with LVEF 65-70% on echocardiogram 09/02/2026. Lexiscan calculated LVEF greater than 75%.
Continue telemetry monitoring.
Continue DVT prophylaxis with heparin 5,000 units subcutaneous every 12 hours as ordered.
Continue mobilization as tolerated.
Nursing Communication
Continue telemetry monitoring.
Notify cardiology for recurrent chest pain, significant ST-segment changes, arrhythmia, hypotension, worsening shortness of breath, or other cardiovascular deterioration.
Continue aspirin 81 mg daily and atorvastatin 80 mg nightly as ordered.
Continue blood pressure monitoring while receiving amlodipine and lisinopril.
Continue mobilization as tolerated.

# AUR FRA - Inpatient Cardiology Progress Note

## Salient Cardiac Features

90-year-old woman with atrial fibrillation, chronic diastolic heart failure, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, valvular heart disease, pulmonary hypertension, hypothyroidism, peripheral vascular disease, and prior permanent pacemaker implantation.

Admitted with gastrointestinal bleeding and acute blood loss anemia while receiving Eliquis for atrial fibrillation. Presentation included dark-colored emesis and black/bloody stools. Hemoglobin declined from approximately 12.1 g/dL as an outpatient in August 2026 to 8.2 g/dL on presentation and subsequently 7.2 g/dL on 09/04/2026. fileciteturn4file0

Eliquis 2.5 mg PO twice daily is currently held because of active GI bleeding. Patient and family were counseled that interruption of anticoagulation increases thromboembolic/stroke risk in the setting of atrial fibrillation.

Atrial fibrillation currently has controlled ventricular response. Continue telemetry monitoring.

Prior successful synchronized electrical cardioversion on 12/29/2022 from atrial fibrillation to sinus rhythm using a single 200-joule biphasic shock after TEE confirmed no left atrial appendage thrombus.

Prior atrial fibrillation therapy included metoprolol 12.5 mg daily and amiodarone 200 mg. These medications are not listed on the current inpatient medication administration record.

Permanent pacemaker previously implanted by Dr. Sovari. Implantation date, pacemaker manufacturer/company, model, and device details are not available in the provided records.

No Watchman device currently documented. Given active GI bleeding and difficulty maintaining long-term anticoagulation, future Watchman candidacy should be considered. Watchman was discussed with the patient and family as a potential minimally invasive stroke-prevention strategy after recovery from the current acute admission, potentially in approximately 1-2 months.

TEE 12/29/2022 demonstrated generous left atrial appendage without thrombus, no PFO, moderate mitral regurgitation, and preserved LV systolic function.

Echocardiogram 05/16/2024 demonstrated normal LV size, mild concentric LV hypertrophy, LVEF 55-60%, mild aortic regurgitation, mild-to-moderate pulmonary hypertension with RVSP 61.51 mmHg, and trivial pericardial effusion.

GI endoscopic evaluation has not yet been performed. Endoscopy/colonoscopy remains important to identify the source of bleeding, including evaluation for possible peptic ulcer disease.

CTA abdomen/pelvis 09/03/2026 demonstrated no active arterial extravasation or venous pooling to indicate active GI bleeding and showed colonic diverticulosis without acute diverticulitis and a small hiatal hernia. fileciteturn4file0

Current cardiac medication includes atorvastatin 20 mg PO daily. Outpatient valsartan and furosemide are being held because of GI bleeding and soft blood pressure. Eliquis remains held.

## SOAP Note

### Subjective

Seen for cardiology evaluation in the setting of acute gastrointestinal bleeding and acute blood loss anemia while receiving chronic Eliquis for atrial fibrillation.

Patient is awake and alert.

Daughter and granddaughter were present for bedside discussion. Spanish translation was provided during discussion.

Discussed that Eliquis must currently be held because of active gastrointestinal bleeding. Patient and family understand that withholding anticoagulation increases the risk of thromboembolic stroke in the setting of atrial fibrillation.

GI evaluation with endoscopy/colonoscopy remains important to determine the source of bleeding, including evaluation for a possible ulcer. These procedures have not yet been performed.

Given the current GI bleeding and difficulty safely maintaining long-term anticoagulation, future candidacy for Watchman left atrial appendage occlusion was discussed. This would be considered after recovery from the acute admission rather than during active bleeding, potentially in approximately 1-2 months.

Will coordinate with the covering hospital physicians during the Labor Day weekend regarding ongoing management.

### Objective

Vitals reviewed elsewhere.

General: Awake, alert, and without acute distress.

Cardiovascular: History of atrial fibrillation with currently controlled ventricular response. Normal S1/S2 with systolic murmur documented at the apex. Trace bilateral lower-extremity edema. Prior permanent pacemaker implantation.

Respiratory: Lungs clear bilaterally without significant rales, rhonchi, or wheezing. Most recently documented oxygen saturation 95% on room air.

Gastrointestinal: Abdomen soft, nontender, and nondistended. Presented with dark-colored emesis and black/bloody stools.

Neurologic: Alert and oriented with no focal neurologic deficit documented.

Laboratory Data 09/04/2026: WBC 5.2 K/µL. Hemoglobin 7.2 g/dL. Hematocrit 21.4%. Platelets 126 K/µL. INR 1.20. Sodium 138 mmol/L. Potassium 3.8 mmol/L. BUN 21 mg/dL. Creatinine 0.80 mg/dL. Magnesium 1.9 mg/dL. Albumin 2.8 g/dL. fileciteturn4file0

CTA Abdomen/Pelvis 09/03/2026: No evidence of active arterial extravasation or venous-phase contrast pooling to suggest active GI bleeding. Colonic diverticulosis without diverticulitis and small hiatal hernia. fileciteturn4file0

Relevant Cardiac Procedures/Studies:

12/29/2022 - Transesophageal echocardiogram demonstrated no left atrial appendage thrombus, absence of PFO, moderate mitral regurgitation, and preserved LV ejection fraction.

12/29/2022 - Successful synchronized electrical cardioversion from atrial fibrillation to sinus rhythm with a single 200-joule biphasic shock.

Permanent pacemaker implantation - Previously performed by Dr. Sovari. Implantation date and manufacturer/company are not available in the provided records.

05/16/2024 - Transthoracic echocardiogram demonstrated LVEF 55-60%, mild concentric LV hypertrophy, mild aortic regurgitation, mild-to-moderate pulmonary hypertension with RVSP 61.51 mmHg, and trivial pericardial effusion.

Coronary angiography/PCI/CABG: No coronary angiography, PCI, or CABG details are available in the provided records.

### Assessment

1. Acute gastrointestinal bleeding with melena/dark emesis while receiving anticoagulation (ICD-10: K92.2)

2. Acute blood loss anemia secondary to gastrointestinal bleeding (ICD-10: D62)

3. Atrial fibrillation with controlled ventricular response, chronic anticoagulation currently interrupted because of active bleeding (ICD-10: I48.91)

4. Chronic diastolic heart failure with preserved LV systolic function (ICD-10: I50.32)

5. Nonrheumatic mitral regurgitation (ICD-10: I34.0)

6. Pulmonary hypertension (ICD-10: I27.20)

7. Essential hypertension (ICD-10: I10)

8. Hyperlipidemia (ICD-10: E78.5)

9. Presence of permanent cardiac pacemaker (ICD-10: Z95.0)

10. Peripheral vascular disease (ICD-10: I73.9)

11. Hypothyroidism (ICD-10: E03.9)

### Plan

High-complexity inpatient medical decision-making performed due to active gastrointestinal bleeding with significant acute blood loss anemia requiring interruption of chronic anticoagulation in a patient with atrial fibrillation and elevated thromboembolic risk, requiring multidisciplinary GI/cardiology management and consideration of alternative long-term stroke-prevention strategy.

GI Bleeding/Acute Blood Loss Anemia: Continue to hold Eliquis during active bleeding. GI evaluation with endoscopy/colonoscopy remains important to identify and treat the bleeding source, including evaluation for possible ulcer. Continue IV pantoprazole infusion as ordered. Continue serial hemoglobin monitoring. Transfusion parameters and further GI management per primary/GI teams.

Atrial Fibrillation/Stroke Prevention: Eliquis 2.5 mg PO twice daily is currently held. Patient and family counseled regarding increased stroke risk while anticoagulation is interrupted. Continue telemetry. Reassess anticoagulation after bleeding source is identified and hemostasis is achieved.

Watchman Consideration: Given GI bleeding and difficulty maintaining long-term anticoagulation, consider evaluation for Watchman left atrial appendage occlusion after recovery from the current acute illness. Procedure discussed with patient and family as a potential future minimally invasive stroke-prevention strategy, potentially in approximately 1-2 months. No Watchman device is currently documented.

Pacemaker: Prior permanent pacemaker implantation by Dr. Sovari. Implantation date, manufacturer, model, and device details are not available in the provided records.

Heart Failure/Hypertension: Outpatient furosemide and valsartan are being held because of GI bleeding and soft blood pressure. Monitor blood pressure, volume status, renal function, and clinical status. Resume cardiovascular therapy as hemodynamics permit.

Valvular/Pulmonary Hypertension History: Prior TEE demonstrated moderate mitral regurgitation. Most recent available echocardiogram from 05/16/2024 demonstrated preserved LVEF 55-60%, mild aortic regurgitation, and mild-to-moderate pulmonary hypertension with RVSP 61.51 mmHg.

Current Medications: Continue atorvastatin 20 mg PO daily, levothyroxine 112 mcg PO daily, donepezil 10 mg PO nightly, IV pantoprazole infusion, and other supportive/PRN medications as ordered. Eliquis is held. Outpatient furosemide and valsartan are held because of current GI bleeding and soft blood pressure. Current inpatient medication list does not include prior metoprolol or amiodarone therapy.

DVT Prophylaxis: Mechanical prophylaxis with SCDs. Avoid pharmacologic DVT prophylaxis during active GI bleeding.

Continue coordination with GI, primary hospital team, patient, and family.

## Nursing Communication

Continue telemetry monitoring for atrial fibrillation and clinically significant rate or rhythm changes.

Eliquis remains held because of active GI bleeding. Do not resume anticoagulation unless specifically directed after reassessment of bleeding status.

Monitor for recurrent hematemesis, melena, hematochezia, hypotension, dizziness, syncope, chest discomfort, dyspnea, or other clinical deterioration.

Continue serial hemoglobin monitoring as ordered and promptly communicate significant decline or symptomatic anemia.

Maintain GI-directed treatment and preparation for endoscopic evaluation as ordered.

Monitor blood pressure and volume status while outpatient valsartan and furosemide remain held.

Continue mobilization as clinically tolerated.
